He starred in the ABC soap opera All My Children (2003ΓÇô2006) and the NBC sports drama series Friday Night Lights (2009ΓÇô2011). He later starred in and produced the HBO television film Fahrenheit 451 (2018), for which he was nominated for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie.

Jordan's film breakthrough came as Oscar Grant in Ryan Coogler's biopic Fruitvale Station (2013), for which his performance received critical praise. He earned further acclaim for his performances in Coogler's subsequent films, including Creed (2015), Black Panther (2018), and Sinners (2025); the latter earned him the Academy Award for Best Actor. Jordan reprised his role of Donnie Creed in Creed II (2018) and Creed III (2023), the latter of which also marked his directorial debut. His other films include Chronicle (2012), That Awkward Moment (2014), Fantastic Four (2015), and Just Mercy (2019).

Aside from filmmaking, Jordan is also a co-owner of Premier League club AFC Bournemouth.

fields.name: T├íta Vega
fields.biography:
T├íta Vega (born October 7, 1951, as Carmen Rosa Vega) is an American singer whose career spans theater, film, and various musical genres.

She began her professional singing career as early as 1963 and later performed in the Los Angeles production of the musical *Hair*. Subsequently, she was a member of the groups Pollution and Earthquire before signing with Motown, where she released several solo albums, including *Full Speed Ahead* (1976), *Totally T├íta* (1977), and *Try My Love* (1978). She became particularly well-known for the song "Get It Up for Love."

As a vocalist, T├íta Vega has collaborated with artists such as Stevie Wonder, Chaka Khan, Michael Jackson, Ray Charles, Madonna, and Elton John. In the film *The Color Purple*, she provided the vocals for the character Shug Avery and was featured on several songs on the soundtrackΓÇöincluding "Miss CelieΓÇÖs Blues (Sister)," which was nominated for an Oscar.

In 1985, she received a Grammy nomination. In 1994, she recorded Spanish-language versions of "Circle of Life" from *The Lion King*. In 2013, she appeared in the documentary *20 Feet from Stardom*, which focuses on backup singers.

Her music has been sampled by artists including Daft Punk, Eminem, and Drake.

fields.name: Kari Wahlgren
fields.biography: Kari K. Wahlgren is an American voice actress who has provided English language voices for dozens of anime titles and video games. She had a live-action role as Tinker Bell in the 2003 Damion Dietz film Neverland. She provided the voice of the supporting character Mindy in the 2008 Walt Disney Animation Studios film Bolt, Haruhara Haruko in Gainax's OVA FLCL, and the computer program Jean in the 2009 television pilot Virtuality. She was interviewed in the 2008 documentary Adventures in Voice Acting. She is currently starring in Disney XD show Kick Buttowski: Suburban Daredevil as Denise Buttowski and the Disney Channel show Fish Hooks as Bea's friend Shellsea.

fields.name: John Ratzenberger
fields.biography:
John Dezso Ratzenberger is an American actor, voice actor, director, producer, writer and entrepreneur. He is one of the most successful actors of all time in terms of box-office receipts. Ratzenberger is best known for portraying Cliff Clavin on the popular comedy series Cheers, for which he earned two Primetime Emmy nominations. He is also known being a voice actor appearing in almost every Pixar Animation Studios feature film, including Hamm in the Toy Story franchise, The Underminer in The Incredibles franchise, and Mack in the Cars franchise.

Ratzenberger began his entertainment career while living in London in the 1970s. He had minor film and television roles throughout the late 70s and early 1980s before creating, and then landing, the role of the know-it-all mailman Cliff Clavin on Cheers, a role he portrayed throughout the show's eleven seasons. His first Pixar role was the voice of Hamm in Toy Story, and he has voiced Pixar characters in films and video games ever since. From 2004 to 2008 he hosted the TV documentary series Made in America.  Outside of acting, he has promoted American entrepreneurship and manufacturing, and campaigned for several Republican candidates.

fields.name: David Lodge
fields.biography:
In an industry without a loss of excellent talent, David is honored in 2018-19 to be working on a vast array of acting projects. Whether it is realistic characters in2019-20 Game of Thrones (NDA), Yarrow the Lead Freelancer in Anthem, Magnus the Russian Baby in Boss Baby! on Netflix, or main characters (Cid, Voyd, Wedge Kincaid, Vyv Dorden, Bahmut) in Final Fantasy -David is, as usual, mostly the chameleon actor --unrecognizable from one character to the next. (Ugh! How is that supposed to help your career?! Ha!)

It's not unusual to hear David voice multiple characters in the same game or animated projects... and in 2019's Battle Wake Arcade Game-David is all four lead Pirate and Ghost voices. Animated movies include Son of Big Foot 2 where David voices a couple of key lead characters.(NDA!) And if you catch Goldie and Bear on Disney Jr.-well you'd be hard pressed... to recognize David having a blast voicing several regulars.

In the last year and half--David is heard in thirty-two video games and a score of cartoons most NDA at this point in time. Needless to say however-many are high profile outlets and producers such as: Disney, Cartoon Network, Dreamworks, WB, Activision, Nick, EA, Bioware, and more. ( Yes, Jiraiya the Toad Sage is busy!)

fields.name: Juno Temple
fields.biography:
Juno Temple (born 21 July 1989) is a British actress. She is known for her roles in the comedy series Ted Lasso (2020ΓÇô2023) and in the fifth season of the crime drama series Fargo (2023ΓÇô2024). She earned Primetime Emmy Award nominations for both as well as a Golden Globe Award nomination for the latter. She also portrayed Teddy Payne in the superhero film Venom: The Last Dance (2024).

Temple, the daughter of film director Julien Temple, began working as a child actress, appearing in Notes on a Scandal (2006), Atonement (2007), The Other Boleyn Girl (2008) and Mr. Nobody (2009). Her subsequent film roles were in The Three Musketeers (2011), The Dark Knight Rises (2012), Magic Magic (2013), Maleficent (2014), Black Mass (2015), Unsane (2018), and Maleficent: Mistress of Evil (2019). Temple received the BAFTA Rising Star Award in 2013. She has also starred in the television series Vinyl (2016), Dirty John (2018ΓÇô2019) and The Offer (2022).

Juno Temple was born in the Hammersmith area of London on 21 July 1989, the daughter of film producer Amanda Pirie and film director Julien Temple. She has two younger brothers, Leo and Felix. Her aunt Nina Temple was the last General Secretary of the Communist Party of Great Britain.  She grew up in Taunton, Somerset, where she attended Enmore Primary School, then Bedales School, returning to Taunton to finish at King's College.

In 2012, she appeared in The Dark Knight Rises, as a "street-smart Gotham girl", and portrayed Diane in the lesbian werewolf tale Jack & Diane. In February 2013, Temple won the EE Rising Star BAFTA Award, voted for by the public. Temple had a supporting role as Deborah Hussey in the true-crime film Black Mass (2015), which starred Johnny Depp; and played Jamie Vine, an A&R assistant for the fictional American Century record company, in the 2016 HBO series Vinyl.

In 2018ΓÇô2019, Temple played a focal role as the protagonist's daughter in the Bravo series Dirty John, which was later acquired by Netflix. In 2020, she won the Best Actress award at the Prague Independent Film Festival for her role in the film Lost Transmissions. In August 2020, Temple began a regular role as Keeley, a former girlfriend of one of the team players and the unofficial team publicist, on the Apple TV+ series Ted Lasso.

In 2022, Temple appeared in the Paramount+ miniseries The Offer, depicting the production of The Godfather. In 2023, Temple appeared in a starring role in the fifth season of the American crime anthology series Fargo.

fields.name: Nathan Greno
fields.biography:
Nathan Greno (born March 22, 1975) is an American film director, story artist, and writer best known as the co-director of Walt Disney Animation Studios' film, Tangled (2010).

Inspired by Disney films since the first grade, Greno started as a young boy writing and drawing comic books and strips. In 1996, during his junior year at Columbus College of Art and Design, he was hired by Walt Disney Feature Animation. He started there as an animation clean-up artist on Mulan (1998). Being creatively unfulfilled, he switched to story development. He then contributed as a story artist on Brother Bear (2003), wrote a screenplay and worked as a story artist on Meet the Robinsons (2007), and supervised the story on Bolt (2008). With the short film Super Rhino (2009), he made his directorial debut. In 2006, he took over a long-in-development project Tangled, based on the fairy tale Rapunzel and chose Byron Howard, with whom he had collaborated on Bolt and Super Rhino, as a directing partner. The film was released in 2010 to a great critical and financial reception, and was followed in 2012 by Greno and Howard-directed short film Tangled Ever After.

Greno had most recently been directing an animated film titled Gigantic. Loosely based on the fairy tale of Jack and the Beanstalk, it was scheduled for a 2020 release. However, in October 2017, it was announced that the film had been shelved. In February 2018, it was announced that Greno had signed a multi-year contract with Skydance Animation to write and direct an animated film titled Swapped, as well as consult on projects in development.

fields.name: John Whittington

John Whittington is an American screenwriter. He is best known for his collaborations with Jared Stern, including The Lego Batman Movie (2017), The Lego Ninjago Movie (2017), and DC League of Super-Pets (2022).

Whittington began his career by writing the screenplays for The Lego Batman Movie and The Lego Ninjago Movie. In July 2017, Whittington was hired to write the script for Boy21. In 2018, he wrote the screenplay for the Netflix film When We First Met. In 2019, he wrote two episodes of the animated series Green Eggs and Ham, based on the Dr. Seuss book of the same name. During reshoots, he rewrote the screenplay for the 2020 film Dolittle. He wrote the DC Comics film DC League of Super-Pets. He gained notability from co-writing the screenplay for the action-adventure comedy film Sonic the Hedgeog 2 and its sequel.

fields.name: Fred Tatasciore
fields.biography:
Frederick "Fred" Tatasciore (born June 13, 1968) is an American voice actor.

Tatasciore was born in New York City, New York in 1967. He was a stand-up comedian before turning over to voice acting.

Tatasciore has portrayed mostly secondary characters as well as monstrous-looking types. He is best known for voicing the Hulk in countless animated roles, including Ultimate Avengers, Next Avengers, Hulk Vs, Marvel Ultimate Alliance 2 and Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes. In video games, he is known for voicing Saren Arterius from the critically acclaimed series Mass Effect and Damon Baird in the Gears of War video game series, and Zeratul from the game StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty. He also voices the character "8" in the Tim Burton-produced film 9 that was released September 9, 2009. His most recent roles are of that as Neftin Prog in Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus, Russian Nikolai Belinski in Call of Duty: World at War and Call of Duty: Black Ops, Tookit in Thundercats, and the Business Cat in the webseries "Our New Electrical Morals", with episodes posted in the Cartoon Hangover YouTube page, administered by Frederator Studios.

There, he worked on films such as *Pocahontas*, *Tarzan*, *Brother Bear*, and *Bolt*. His first project at Disney was *Pocahontas*, on which he served as an Assistant Editor. Later, he workedΓÇöamong other rolesΓÇöas Supervising Editor on the animated film *Tangled*, assisting the directors in developing the project from initial sketches and storyboards through to the finished theatrical release.

In 1994, Mertens also received an Emmy Award for sound editing on the Nickelodeon series *RockoΓÇÖs Modern Life*.

He has animated on a bunch of feature films including How To Train Your Dragon, and Rise of The Guardians, The Bee Movie, Flushed Away, Shark Tale, Osmosis Jones, Eight Crazy Nights, Joseph the King of Dreams.  "One of the proudest professional moments I've had was being the supervising animator for Toothless in the first How To Train Your Dragon movie and sitting in the theater, feeling the whole audience hold their breath  as Hiccup and Toothless touch for the first time, was simply unforgettable. "

fields.name: John Lasseter
fields.biography:
John Alan Lasseter is an American film director, producer, screenwriter, animator, voice actor, and the head of animation at Skydance Animation. He was previously the chief creative officer of Pixar Animation Studios, Walt Disney Animation Studios, and Disneytoon Studios, as well as the Principal Creative Advisor for Walt Disney Imagineering.

Lasseter's first job was with The Walt Disney Company, where he became an animator. Next, he joined Lucasfilm, where he worked on the then-groundbreaking use of CGI animation. After Lucasfilm became Pixar in 1986, Lasseter oversaw all of Pixar's films and associated projects as executive producer and he directed Toy Story, A Bug's Life, Toy Story 2, Cars, "Toy Story 3" and "Cars 2".

He has won two Academy Awards, for Animated Short Film (Tin Toy), as well as a Special Achievement Award (Toy Story).

fields.name: Mila Jaymes
fields.biography:
Mila Jaymes is an American child actress, singer, and dancer. Jaymes began performing at age 2, and she has trained with respected coaches and institutions, including the Le Blanc School of Acting in New York and Los Angeles, Technique Prep (NY/NJ), and Studio 19 Dance Complex, studying voice, acting technique, tap, jazz, musical theatre, lyrical, contemporary, ballet, and acro. In addition to her performance training, she is an accomplished gymnast and tumbler with skills in contortion and aerial techniques. She has participated in major dance conventions such as Radix, Nuvo, Intrigue, DanceMakers, and ASH.

Jaymes made her Broadway debut as Baby June in the revival of┬áGypsy┬áin 2024 at the Majestic Theatre, directed by George C. Wolfe and starring Audra McDonald. She previously made her stage debut as Cindy Lou Who in the Broadway National Tour of┬áDr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas! The Musical. Her additional theatre credits include Shanti in The Jungle Book, an Oompa Loompa in Willy Wonka, Sherry the Fox in Winnie the Pooh, and a Mouse in The Nutcracker at the Benedum Center. She has also appeared as a soloist in cabaret and concert performances in New York City and Pittsburgh, including engagements at Don't Tell Mama, presented by Voices to End Hunger, and at the Bhyam Theater.

On television, Jaymes has supporting roles in┬áStuart Fails to Save the Universe┬á(2026) and as Charli in the Untitled┬á'The Punisher' Special Presentation (2026). Her work extends to national commercial campaigns, including Target's 2025 holiday commercial directed by Jon M. Chu. She is represented theatrically by Osbrink, commercially and in voiceover by The Osbrink Agency, and for dance by BLOC Talent Agency, with additional modelling representation through State Management.

Other television appearances include Fringe, Party Down, How to Make It in America, and Empire. In film, he had roles in Shaft (2000), Super (2010), The Spectacular Now (2013), Beautiful Boy (2018), Prospect (2018), and To Leslie (2022). Royo was born in the Bronx, New York of African American and Cuban heritage. He attended Mount Saint Michael Academy in The Bronx from 1982 - 1986. Royo is married to Jane Choi and has a daughter, Stella.

fields.name: Mugga
fields.biography:
Mugga, a Brooklyn native, is known for bringing a great sense of comedy to her dramatic roles. Her journey began at a young age where she studied acting with such instructors as Tracey Moore, Joanna Beckson, Paul Calderon, and more.

On a dare, she tried her hand at stand-up comedy. It didn't take long for her to catch the eye of Def Comedy Jam scout Bob Sumner. She quickly received a slew of high-profile stand-up gigs which gave her a big break onto the comedy scene. (These included DEF COMEDY JAM, SHOWTIME AT THE APOLLO, BET'S COMIC VIEW 3X, and BBC'S CLUB CLASS.)

Receiving glowing reviews (including the New York Times), she soon went on tour with DEF JAM as well as COMEDY TROUPE SWG (a UK Based Comedy Troupe), SISTAHS WITH GAGS, etc. All of the Stand-Up comedy success gave her entertainment career a push to new heights and she was able to return to her acting endeavors.

Her love of acting and training soon paid off when she auditioned for Lee Daniels' Oscar winning film Precious and landed the role as the ever-memorable restaurant worker who Precious 'stole the chicken from'.

She continued to hone her craft while keeping active in the stand-up comedy world. It was then in the ground-breaking Netflix Original Series Orange Is The New Black that she landed her SAG-award winning role of Reema Pell. As her acting career skyrocketed, she took to the skies with a major recurring role on NBC's cult hit Manifest as Bethany Collins - the lovable attendant from that fateful flight.

Mugga continues to consistently book major roles in such high-profile TV shows as Bull, Power, Homeland, Blue Bloods, High Maintenance, and many more. She can also be seen on the big screen in Blumhouse' dystopian action franchise The First Purge!

As she continues to navigate the worlds of acting and comedy, she keeps her eye on the prize - ever keeping in mind her favorite quote, "The Best Is Yet To Come".

Kevin Feige┬á(/╦êfa╔¬╔íi/┬áFY-ghee; born June 2, 1973) is an American film and television producer. He has been the president of┬áMarvel Studios┬áand the primary producer of the┬áMarvel Cinematic Universe┬á(MCU) franchise since 2007.┬áThe films he has produced have a combined worldwide box office gross of over┬á$31┬ábillion, making him the┬áhighest-grossing producer of all time, with┬áAvengers: Endgame┬á(2019) becoming the┬áhighest-grossing film┬áat its release.

Feige is a member of the┬áProducers Guild of America. In 2018, he was nominated for the┬áAcademy Award for Best Picture┬áfor producing┬áBlack Panther, the first superhero film to receive that honour and the first film in the MCU to win an Academy Award. fields.name: Brad Winderbaum
fields.biography:
Brad Winderbaum is an American producer and the Head of Marvel Television, Animation, Comics & Franchise at Marvel Studios. He was formerly a VP of Production & Development at the company.

Winderbaum joined Marvel Studios during the production of the company's first feature,┬áIron Man, as an assistant to Louis D'Esposito . He played a role in developing the studio's immersive marketing, contributing to the creation of behind-the-scenes documentaries and interactive campaigns for films such as┬áIron Man 2 (2010),┬áThor (2011),┬áCaptain America: The First Avenger (2011), and┬áThe Avengers (2012).

In his current role, Winderbaum has been a driving force behind Marvel Studios' expansion into television and animation. He has overseen the development and production every TV series and special since What If...? (2021). Under his leadership, Marvel Studios introduced a new sub-banner of its Marvel Television banner called Marvel Spotlight, which is meant for select series that explore more grounded, character-driven stories and have little to no impact on the larger MCU narrative.

fields.name: Louis D'Esposito
fields.biography:
Louis D'Esposito is an Executive Producer and Co-President of Marvel Studios. D'Esposito was born in 1958 in the Bronx, New York, and began his film career in the early 1990s. He started his career as an associate producer and first assistant director on various Hollywood productions, including┬áAnother You┬á(1991),┬áBasic Instinct┬á(1992),┬áDudley Do-Right┬á(1999),┬áS.W.A.T.┬á(2003), and┬áThe Pursuit of Happyness┬á(2006).

In 2006, D'Esposito joined Marvel Studios, making his debut as unit production manager and executive producer on┬áIron Man┬á(2008). He continued in these roles on┬áCaptain America: The First Avenger┬áand various Marvel One-Shots. Over time, he became a central figure in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's growth, executive producing virtually every MCU film since┬áIron Man┬á(with the sole exception of┬áThe Incredible Hulk) and guiding franchises including┬áCaptain America,┬áGuardians of the Galaxy,┬áBlack Panther, and┬áAvengers, collectively earning over $29 billion at the global box office.

Beyond production, D'Esposito has directed Marvel One-ShotsΓÇöItemΓÇ»47┬á(2012) and┬áAgentΓÇ»Carter┬á(2013)ΓÇöthe latter laying the groundwork for the┬áAgent Carter┬áTV series.

He advanced to co-president of Marvel Studios in 2009, sharing leadership with Kevin Feige. In that capacity, he oversees feature film and streaming series development and production, including titles like┬áWandaVision,┬áThe Falcon and the Winter Soldier,┬áLoki,┬áMs.ΓÇ»Marvel,┬áIronheart,┬áYour Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man,┬áDaredevil: Born Again, and numerous other projects.

He has received Primetime Emmy nominations for WandaVision┬áin 2021 (Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series) and for┬áWhat IfΓÇª?┬áin 2022 (Outstanding Animated Program). In 2024, he was nominated for Outstanding Animated Program again for┬áXΓÇæMen ΓÇÖ97┬á(Season 1 Episode 5, ΓÇ£Remember ItΓÇ¥). Additionally, he earned nominations from the Television Academy for┬áThe Falcon and the Winter Soldier,┬áLoki, and┬áEcho┬áin technical categories, including costumes, sound mixing, and visual effects. Beyond industry awards, he was honoured in January 2024 with the inaugural ΓÇ£Renaissance AwardΓÇ¥ from the Russo BrothersΓÇÖ Italian American Filmmaker Forum in recognition of his contributions to ItalianΓÇæAmerican heritage and the entertainment world.

fields.name: John Romita Sr.
fields.biography:
John Victor Romita┬á(/r╔Ö╦êmi╦Ét╔Ö/; January 24, 1930 ΓÇô June 12, 2023) was an American comic book artist best known for his work on┬áMarvel Comics'┬áThe Amazing Spider-Man┬áand co-creating characters including┬áMary Jane Watson, the┬áPunisher,┬áKingpin,┬áWolverine, and┬áLuke Cage. Romita was the father of┬áJohn Romita Jr., a comic book artist, and the husband of Virginia Romita, who was Marvel's traffic manager for many years.

His first comics work was in 1949 as a┬ághost artist for┬áTimely Comics, the precursor to Marvel, through which Romita met editor-in-chief┬áStan Lee. In 1951, Romita began drawing horror, war, and romance comics for┬áAtlas Comics┬á(previously Timely) and also drew his first superhero work, a 1950s revival of┬áCaptain America. He worked exclusively for┬áDC Comics┬áfrom 1958 to 1965 and was the artist for many of their romance comics. During these years, Romita further developed his ability to draw beautiful women, for which he later became well-known.

Romita joined Marvel in 1965, initially drawing┬áDaredevil┬ácomics. In 1966, when┬áSpider-Manartist and co-creator┬áSteve Ditko┬áleft Marvel, Romita was chosen by writer Lee as the new artist for┬áAmazing Spider-Man. Within a year of Romita becoming the Spider-Man artist,┬áThe Amazing Spider-Man┬árose from Marvel's second-best-selling title to the company's top-seller. Romita brought a new romance style to Spider-Man comics that soon became the new design for the character. In June 1973, Romita was promoted to Marvel's art director and heavily influenced the look of Marvel comics throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Romita was inducted into the┬áWill Eisner Comic Book Hall of Fame┬áin 2002.

Gerard Francis Conway┬á(September 10, 1952 - April 27, 2026) was an American comic book writer, comic book editor, science fiction writer,┬áscreenwriter, television writer, and television producer. At┬áDC Comics, he is known for co-creating the┬ásuperheroes┬áFirestorm,┬áPower Girl,┬áJason Todd, and the villain┬áKiller Croc and for writing the┬áJustice League of America┬áfor eight years. Conway wrote the first major, modern-day┬áintercompany crossover,┬áSuperman vs. the Amazing Spider-Man.

fields.name: Jan Jericho

Jan Michael Jericho (born 1978) is a German-born supervising art director and production designer whose career bridges European cinema and major American television. Born in T├╝bingen, Germany, he earned a MasterΓÇÖs degree in Stage and Costume Design from the State Academy of Arts and Design in Stuttgart. Also, he studied history at Eberhard Karls University in T├╝bingen. Fluent in German and English, with working knowledge of French, Jericho began his career in Germany, working on feature films, commercials, and television projects in roles ranging from set designer to concept artist. His early work included production design for Picco (2010), which gained acclaim at the Max-Oph├╝ls-Film Festival and earned a Cam├⌐ra dΓÇÖOr nomination at Cannes. He also contributed as a graphic artist and concept illustrator on international films such as Anonymous (2011), Inglourious Basterds (2009), The Three Musketeers (2011), Cloud Atlas (2012), Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters (2013), and Valkyrie (2008).

After moving into U.S. television, Jericho worked across acclaimed series, including Boardwalk Empire (2010ΓÇô2014), The Knick (2014ΓÇô2015), Master of None (2015ΓÇô2021), Daredevil (2015ΓÇô2018), The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel (2017ΓÇô2023), Crashing (2017ΓÇô2019), Odd Mom Out (2015ΓÇô2017), The Night Agent (2023ΓÇô), and ├ëtoile (upcoming). His artistry has been recognised extensively by the Art Directors Guild. He has won the Excellence in Production Design Award twice for The Marvelous Mrs. MaiselΓÇöin 2019 for the episodes ΓÇ£SimoneΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£WeΓÇÖre Going to the Catskills!ΓÇ¥ and in 2020 for ΓÇ£ItΓÇÖs Comedy or CabbageΓÇ¥ and episode 308ΓÇöshared with collaborators including Bill Groom, Neil Prince, and Ellen Christiansen. His additional ADG nominations span multiple high-profile productions: in 2023 for The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel (ΓÇ£Maisel vs. Lennon: The Cut ContestΓÇ¥ and episode 408), in 2018 for Master of None (ΓÇ£Le Nozze,ΓÇ¥ ΓÇ£Thanksgiving,ΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£Amarsi Un P├▓ΓÇ¥), in 2016 for The Knick (ΓÇ£Ten KnotsΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£The Best with the Best to Get the BestΓÇ¥), and in 2015, 2014, and 2013 for various episodes of Boardwalk Empire. He was also nominated in 2012 for Anonymous in the Period Film category, sharing recognition with Sebastian T. Krawinkel, Stephan O. Gessler, Stefan Speth, and Sabine Engelberg.

fields.name: Robert Elswit

fields.name: Annika Pergament
fields.biography:
Annika Pergament is the Senior Business Anchor for NY1 and Time Warner Cable's other newschannels across the United States. In her role, Pergament leads the business news coverage from the New York Stock Exchange.

As a reporter for NY1 in 1994, Pergament covered politics and later City Hall and the Manhattan beat. In 2001, she joined WCBS-TV as the consumer reporter for the stationΓÇÖs Troubleshooter segment and was a regular contributor to the Early Show. Pergament rejoined NY1 in 2002 as Business Anchor and producer of the Fortune Business Report. From 2002-2009, she also worked as a guest anchor on  Court TV, and later TruTVΓÇÖs In Session, hosting Newsbreaks and live trial coverage.

She has also had recurring role as a news anchor on HBOΓÇÖs The Sopranos and has appeared in Gossip Girl, Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps, Laws of Attraction, Head of State, Maid in Manhattan, Analyze That, and The Yards.

Michael Shaw is a production designer. He began his artistic journey studying painting, sculpture, and film at the Rhode Island School of Design, where he earned a BFA cum laude. His transition into production design was sparked when a short film he worked on,┬áThe Room┬á(1993), won top honours at Cannes, Sundance, and MoMA. That early success solidified his conviction that production design offered the ability to unify all his creative passions in one discipline.

In the realm of independent cinema, Shaw lent his design sensibilities to a number of emotionally resonant films. His credits include┬áHeavy┬á(1995), James Mangold's feature debut;┬áBoys Don't Cry┬á(1999), which earned Hilary Swank her first Academy Award;┬áYou Can Count on Me┬á(2000), starring Laura Linney and Mark Ruffalo;┬áA Home at the End of the World┬á(2004), based on Michael Cunningham's novel;┬áAugust Rush┬á(2007);┬áCop Out┬á(2010);┬áThe Private Lives of Pippa Lee┬á(2009);┬áThe Night Listener┬á(2006);┬áTrust┬á(2010);┬áThe English Teacher┬á(2013);┬áThe Other Woman┬á(2009);┬áDouble Whammy┬á(2001);┬áPeople I Know┬á(2002); and┬áAvailable Light┬á(1990).

Shaw's television work has been equally impactful, with defining runs on several celebrated series. He served as production designer on┬áThe Big C┬á(2010ΓÇô2013),┬áOrange Is the New Black┬á(2013ΓÇô2015, seasons 1ΓÇô3),┬áBillions┬á(2016ΓÇô2017, seasons 1ΓÇô2),┬áLodge 49┬á(2018ΓÇô2019, seasons 1ΓÇô2), and the limited series┬áThe Staircase┬á(2022).

fields.name: Bhushan Kumar

fields.name: Ayesha Raza Mishra

She soon took to performing on stage after training under the guidance of Amal and Nissar Allana at the Dramatic Art and Design Academy in New Delhi. is an Indian fashion designer, costume stylist, entrepreneur, and film producer. He studied at Elphinstone College and entered the Hindi film industry in 1990 as a costume designer with Swarg. fields.name: Tanishk Bagchi

Tanishk Bagchi is an Indian music producer, composer, singer and lyrics writer. Hailing from Kolkata, Bagchi was born to musicians Nandakumar Bagchi and Sharmistha Das. He attended Frank Anthony Public School and Scottish Church Collegiate School, Kolkata.

He won the IIFA 2018 for best music composer for the film Badrinath Ki Dulhania. He made his debut in Bollywood with the song "Banno" composed with Vayu Srivastava from the film Tanu Weds Manu Returns in 2015. Before composing for films, he produced and arranged music for TV shows. Since then, he has composed several hit songs including the Badrinath Ki Dulhania title track. fields.name: Alex Innocenti

fields.name: Ranveer Singh
fields.biography:
Ranveer Singh Bhavnani (born 6 July 1985) is an Indian film actor who appears in Hindi films. After completing a bachelor's degree from Indiana University, Bloomington, Singh returned to India to pursue a career in film. He made his acting debut in 2010 with a leading role in Yash Raj Films' romantic comedy Band Baaja Baaraat. The film emerged as a critical and commercial success, earning Singh a Filmfare Award in the Best Male Debut category.

Singh went on to star in the romantic drama Lootera (2013), Sanjay Leela Bhansali's tragic romance Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), his biggest commercial successes to that point, and in the action-drama Gunday (2014). In 2015, he starred in the ensemble comedy-drama Dil Dhadakne Do (2015), and portrayed Bajirao in the historical romance Bajirao Mastani, one of the highest-grossing Bollywood films, for which he garnered critical acclaim and won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor.

fields.name: Arjun Rampal
fields.biography: Arjun Rampal (born November 26, 1972) is an Indian actor, model, and producer. His accolades include a National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor and a Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award.

fields.name: R. Madhavan
fields.biography:
Ranganathan Madhavan (born 1 June 1970) is an Indian actor, writer and film producer. He has been described as one of the few actors in India who is able to achieve pan-Indian appeal, appearing in films from seven different languages. Madhavan has received two Filmfare Awards, an award from the Tamil Nadu State Film Awards alongside recognition and nominations from other organisations.  Madhavan began his acting career with television guest appearances, including a role on the Zee TV prime-time soap opera Banegi Apni Baat in 1996. After appearing in commercials and in small roles, he later gained recognition in the Tamil film industry through Mani Ratnam's successful romance film Alaipayuthey (2000).

In addition to his acting career, Madhavan has worked as a writer on his films, hosted television programmes and has been a prominent celebrity endorser for brands and products.[5] He has also worked as a film producer, first making Evano Oruvan with Leukos Films, before setting up Tricolour Films to produce Saala Khadoos (2016). Madhavan is noted for his philanthropic activities and promotes various causes such as environment, health and education. He is particularly vocal about the protection of animals and was awarded PETA's Person of the Year recognition in 2012.

fields.name: Sanjay Dutt
fields.biography: Sanjay Dutt (born 29 July 1959) is an Indian film actor and producer who works in Hindi cinema in addition to a few Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, and Punjabi films. Dutt is the son of Hindi film stars Sunil and Nargis Dutt. He made his debut in 1981. Known for his versatile roles, style and intensity, he has often portrayed flawed heroes on screen.

fields.name: Sara Arjun
fields.biography: Sara Arjun (born 15 June 2005) is an Indian actress who has appeared in films, a series of commercials, and a short Hindi film before the age of six. In 2010, she was signed to portray a lead role in A. L. Vijay's Tamil drama film Deiva Thirumagal, portraying the role of a six-year-old daughter whose father was a  mentally challenged adult with the maturity of a six-year-old boy. The  film opened to critical and commercial acclaim, with Sara's performance receiving praise from film critics. She has since worked on Tamil and Hindi films, winning positive reviews for her portrayals, particularly for her role in Vijay's Saivam.

fields.name: Julie Schubert
fields.biography: Julie Schubert is an American casting director based in New York.

fields.name: Rakesh Bedi
fields.biography:
Rakesh Bedi (born 1 December 1954) is an Indian film, stage and television actor. He is most known for his comedy roles in films such as Chashme Buddoor (1981), the television series, Yeh Jo Hai Zindagi (1984), Shrimaan Shrimati (1995) and Yes Boss (1999ΓÇô2009).

Bedi started his film career as a supporting actor in the 1979 film Hamare Tumhare, starring Sanjeev Kumar, and then went on to act in over 150 films and several TV serials. Some of his most memorable roles were in the 1981 film Chashme Buddoor with Farooq Shaikh, Ek Duuje Ke Liye and Ravi Baswani and in the TV sitcoms Shrimaan Shrimati (1995), Yes Boss and Yeh Jo Hai Zindagi (1984), written by Sharad Joshi and directed by Kundan Shah. He had a minor role in Gulzar's Mere Apne, and has acted in a number of Punjabi movies, including Main Tu Assi Tussi.

fields.name: Arjan Panwar
fields.biography:
Samarth Panwar (born 5 July 2009), known professionally as Arjan Panwar, is an Indian actor, singer, songwriter, rapper, model and businessman. He is widely known for his contribution in Haryanvi cinema and music industry.

He was born on 5 July 2009 in Kaimla village of Haryana, India in a Ror family of Dankher clan to businessman Sandeep Panwar and Asha Devi. He is the elder brother of Ishika Panwar, who is an actress and dancer. As a child, Panwar studied at Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Sagga, Karnal.

fields.name: Manav Gohil
fields.biography: Manav Gohil is an Indian actor. He has been active in the Hindi film industry for more than a decade and is best known for his roles in Hindi television shows, including the soap opera Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii, the dance reality show Nach Baliye 2, the crime drama C.I.D., the drama Shaadi Mubarak and Tenali Rama. He is also known for Super 30 (2019), Josh (2000) and Baaghi 3 (2020).

fields.name: Danish Pandor
fields.biography: Danish Pandor (born 22 December 1987) is an Indian actor and former model. Pandor gained fame for playing the mobster Uzair Baloch in the 2025 espionage thriller Dhurandhar.

fields.name: Indeevar
fields.biography: Shyamalal Babu Rai, known professionally as Indeevar (also credited as Indiwar and Indeewar), (1 January 1924 ΓÇô 27 February 1997) was one of the leading Hindi film lyricists from the 1960s then through1990s

fields.name: Suvinder Vicky
fields.biography: Suvinder Vicky was born on March 4, 1973 in Sirsa, Haryana, India. He is an actor, known for Kohrra (2023), Milestone (2020) and Udta Punjab (2016). He is married to Gursharan Kaur Maan.

fields.name: Brad Baruh
fields.biography:
Bradford Baruh is a director and an executive producer.

He is best known for directing most of Marvel StudiosΓÇÖ Assembled documentaries. He also worked as a visual effects producer on Marvel One-Shot: The Consultant and Marvel One-Shot: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Thor's Hammer and a co-producer on Marvel One-Shot: Item 47 and Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter.

fields.name: Ayushmann Khurrana
fields.biography:
Ayushmann Khurrana is an Indian actor, poet, singer, and television host. He has established a career in Hindi cinema and is the recipient of several awards, including two Filmfare Awards.

Khurrana won the second season of reality television show MTV Roadies in 2004 and ventured into an anchoring career. He made his film debut in 2012 with the romantic comedy Vicky Donor. His performance earned him several accolades including the Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut. Following a brief setback, he starred in the commercially and critically successful romance Dum Laga Ke Haisha. Khurrana went on to establish himself with the comedies Bareilly Ki Barfi (2017), Shubh Mangal Saavdhan (2017), and Badhaai Ho (2018), and the thriller Andhadhun (2018).

In addition to acting, Khurrana has sung for all his films, including the song "Pani Da Rang", which earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer.

fields.name: Sara Ali Khan
fields.biography: Sara Ali Khan is an Indian actress who works in Hindi films. A member of the Pataudi family, she is the daughter of actors Saif Ali Khan and Amrita Singh and the paternal grandchild of Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi and Sharmila Tagore. After graduating from Columbia University, Khan ventured into acting by playing the leading lady in the 2018 films Kedarnath and Simmba.

fields.name: Yami Gautam Dhar
fields.biography:
Yami Gautam Dhar (n├⌐e Gautam; born 28 November 1988) is an Indian actress who works in Hindi films. The daughter of film director Mukesh Gautam, she began her career as a model, and starred in television soap operas such as Chand Ke Paar Chalo (2008ΓÇô2009) and Yeh Pyar Na Hoga Kam (2009ΓÇô2010). After making her film debut in the Kannada film Ullasa Utsaha (2010), she had her first Hindi film release in the comedy-drama Vicky Donor (2012), which won her the Zee Cine Award for Best Female Debut.

Gautam earned acclaim for her supporting roles in the thrillers Badlapur (2015) and Kaabil (2017), and greater success came for starring in the war film Uri: The Surgical Strike and the satire Bala (both 2019). She starred in the streaming films Bhoot Police (2021), A Thursday (2022), Dasvi (2022), and Chor Nikal Ke Bhaga (2023), and had further commercial success in the comedy film OMG 2 (2023) and the political thriller Article 370 (2024).

She is married to filmmaker Aditya Dhar.

fields.name: Tigmanshu Dhulia
fields.biography: Tigmanshu Dhulia is an Indian film dialogue writer, director, actor, screenwriter, producer and casting director known for his works in Hindi cinema and Television.

fields.name: Vijay Raaz
fields.biography:
Vijay Raaz is an Indian film actor. His breakthrough hit came when he played the role of Dubeyji in the movie Monsoon Wedding. Since then, Raaz has been cast in small, often comedic roles, in many Hindi movies, often depicting the character of a common man.

Raaz was born and raised in Delhi where he attended Kirori Mal College. While at college he was a part of the dramatic society The Players. He also appeared in plays at the National School of Drama. He decided to focus on a film career and moved to Mumbai where he received a role in Ram Gopal Varma's Jungle. Naseeruddin Shah had seen him perform at the NSD and recommended him to Mahesh Mathai for Bhopal Express and to Mira Nair for Monsoon Wedding. After the success of Monsoon Wedding Raaz received many roles. His first mainstream film cast as the leading actor was Raghu Romeo, a box office success where Raaz depicts the life of a confused lower-class Indian fellow.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Vijay Raaz, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia

fields.name: Bosco Martis
fields.biography: BoscoΓÇôCaesar is an Indian choreographer duo who work in Bollywood. They are Bosco Martis and Caesar Gonsalves, who have together worked on 200 songs and about 75 films. They run the Bosco Caesar Dance Company in Brampton, Scarborough, Mumbai, Phoolbagan, and Salt Lake in Kolkata.

fields.name: Vijendar Singh
fields.biography: Vijender Singh Beniwal (born 29 October 1985) is an Indian professional boxer, actor and politician of Bharatiya Janata Party. As an amateur, he won a bronze medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first Indian boxer to win an Olympic medal. He also won bronze medals at the 2009 World Championships and the 2010 Commonwealth Games, as well as silver medals at the 2006 and 2014 Commonwealth Games, all in the middleweight division.

fields.name: Akshaye Khanna
fields.biography:
Akshay Khanna (born 28 March 1975) is an Indian film actor. He made his acting debut in 1997 with Himalay Putra which was produced by his father Vinod Khanna. Since then he has been featured in several critically and commercially acclaimed films. Akshaye has been a recipient of Filmfare Awards twice.

His most popular films include Border (1997), Taal (1999), Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Hulchul (2004), Race (2008), Dhurandhar (2025) among others. He was critically acclaimed for his performance in Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Humraaz (2002), Gandhi, My Father (2007) and Dhurandhar (2025)

Akshaye Khanna had a four year gap from his acting career following his role in Gali Gali Chor Hai. He returned in 2016 as an antagonistic character in the film Dishoom.

fields.name: Aditya Dhar
fields.biography: Aditya Dhar (born 12 March 1983) is an Indian director, screenwriter, producer and lyricist who works in Hindi cinema. He made his directorial debut with the 2019 war film Uri: The Surgical Strike, which was a critical and commercial success, becoming the 4th highest-grossing Indian film of the year and earning Dhar the National Film Award for Best Direction. He then directed the Dhurandhar series (2025-2026), a spy action thriller duology; both films in the series emerged as being among the highest-grossing Indian films of all time, earning Dhar widespread recognition across the Indian film industry. Dhar's films are known for their nationalistic themes, which have divided critics; commentators have contrastingly described his works as patriotic or jingoistic.

fields.name: Jyoti Deshpande
fields.biography:
President ΓÇô Jio Studios (Media & Content Business ΓÇô Reliance Industries Ltd)

Jyoti Deshpande is one of IndiaΓÇÖs foremost media and entertainment leaders, with over 30 years of experience across content creation, distribution, media strategy, and digital transformation. As President of the Media & Content Business at Reliance Industries Limited, she spearheads the vision and operations of Jio Studios, IndiaΓÇÖs No.1 content studio and a market leader she built from inception. Her ability to blend creative instincts with business acumen has made her a pioneer in consolidating IndiaΓÇÖs fragmented content industry, often referred to as the ΓÇ£JioficationΓÇ¥ of Indian entertainment.

Under her leadership, Jio Studios has delivered unprecedented box office success, led by the blockbuster Dhurandhar duology that has grossed over Γé╣3000 crore ($330 million) worldwide, setting new global benchmarks, securing a place among the top 10 highest-grossing films worldwide in 2026. Jio Studios also holds the rare distinction of producing IndiaΓÇÖs highest-grossing Hindi films for three consecutive yearsΓÇöStree 2 (2024), Dhurandhar (2025), and Dhurandhar The Revenge (2026), cementing its leadership in theatrical entertainment.

This sustained momentum extends across a diverse and culturally resonant slate of films, including Laapataa Ladies (IndiaΓÇÖs official entry to the Oscars 2025), Stree, Article 370, Shaitaan, and Singham Again, among others. In under a decade, Jio Studios has produced over 200 films and web series in multiple Indian languages, with over 60 titles winning more than 500 awards reflecting JyotiΓÇÖs commitment to scale, inclusion, and storytelling with cultural impact.  Beyond theatrical success, Jyoti has driven Jio StudiosΓÇÖ strong expansion into the digital ecosystem. In 2025 alone, the studio delivered a robust slate of 12 OTT releases across genres, including Mrs., Dhoom Dhaam, Bhagwat, Saali Mohabbat and Baramulla, reinforcing its platform-agnostic content strategy.  The acquisition of a majority stake in Oscar-winning Sikhya Entertainment further strengthens Jio StudiosΓÇÖ global ambitions and its ΓÇÿMake in India, Show the WorldΓÇÖ vision.

Beyond creative vision, Jyoti brings unique perspectives on navigating media convergence, strategic investments, and digital disruption in emerging markets. As former CEO of Viacom18, she remains the only woman to have led a ΓÇÿBig 4ΓÇÖ Indian media company. Her extensive leadership experience spans board roles at Network18, Balaji Telefilms, JioSaavn, and Sikhya Entertainment.

A respected industry voice, Jyoti has also played a pivotal role in policy and advocacy as Chairperson of FICCI Media & Entertainment Committee. A BAFTA member, she consistently features among Fortune India and Business TodayΓÇÖs Most Powerful Women in Business.  With her multi-functional experience from nurturing content to global platform partnerships, Jyoti brings a rich, hands-on industry perspective to conversations on leadership, storytelling, media & entertainment value chain, gender and diversity, and the future of media.

fields.name: Saumya Tandon
fields.biography:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Saumya Tandon (3 November 1984) is an Indian actress. Recently she co-hosted Zor Ka Jhatka: Total Wipeout (Based on the Wipeout format) with Shah Rukh Khan in 2011. She was the host for Dance India Dance. She starred in the Imtiaz Ali directed movie Jab We Met, starring Shahid Kapoor and Kareena Kapoor, where she plays the role of Kareena's sister, Roop. She is also known for her role in the Sony TV aired soap Aisa Des Hai Mera, where she plays the role of a half-Brit girl named Rusty.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Saumya Tandon, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Justin Jose
fields.biography: Justin Jose is an Indian Sound Engineer and Sound Mixer. He has worked in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and Malayalam films.

fields.name: Irshad Kamil
fields.biography: Irshad Kamil is an Indian poet and lyricist. His songs appear in Bollywood films including Jab We Met, Chameli, Love Aaj Kal, Rockstar, Aashiqui 2, Raanjhanaa, Highway, Tamasha, and Jab Harry Met Sejal.

fields.name: Jasmine Sandlas
fields.biography: Jasmine Kaur Sandlas is an Indian playback singer, television personality, performer, songwriter. who mainly sings Punjabi songs. She was also featured on the TEDx Talks, MTV Coke Studio and Spoken Word platforms. Jasmine Sandlas is an Independent Artist.

fields.name: Jack Reynor
fields.biography: Jack Reynor (born 23 January 1992) is an American-born Irish actor. He won the IFTA Award for Best Lead Actor ΓÇô Film for his performance in What Richard Did (2012), and Best Supporting Actor for Sing Street (2016). His other notable films include Transformers: Age of Extinction (2014), Glassland (2014), Macbeth (2015), Midsommar (2019) and Lee Cronin's The Mummy (2026), as well as the television series Strange Angel (2018ΓÇô19) and The Peripheral (2022).

fields.name: Laia Costa
fields.biography:
Laia Costa (Catalan: [╦êlaj╔Ö ╦êk╔öst╔Ö]; born February 18, 1985) is a Spanish actress. She is best known for starring in the critically acclaimed one-shot German thriller Victoria (2015), for which she received several accolades, including a German Film Award for Best Actress, becoming the first foreign actress to win a Lola and a BAFTA Rising Star Award nomination. After initial minor television roles in Spain, including an appearance in Polseres vermelles (2013), she went on to star in the romantic dramas Newness (2017) and Only You (2018), the horror thriller Piercing (2018), the romantic comedy Duck Butter (2018), and the multi-narrative drama Life Itself (2018).

Costa has also appeared in the television series Foodie Love (2019), Devils (2020), and the science fiction anthology Soulmates (2020). She gained widespread acclaim in Spain for her portrayal of Amaia in Lullaby (2022), becoming the most acclaimed performance of the awards season, winning the Goya Award for Best Actress, along with a Feroz Award, a Forqu├⌐ Award, and a Platino Award. She later starred in the romantic drama Un amor (2023), earning her a second Platino Award, and portrayed Moghedien in the Amazon Prime Video series The Wheel of Time (2023ΓÇô2025).

fields.name: May Calamawy
fields.biography:
May Calamawy (born October 28, 1986) is an Egyptian-Palestinian actress. She is best known for her role in the Hulu television series Ramy as Dena Hassan. She also appeared in the Disney+ series Moon Knight.

Description above from the Wikipedia article May Calamawy, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Natalie Grace
fields.biography: Natalie Grace is an American actress. She is best known for her role as Kate in the horror film Lee Cronin's The Mummy (2026).

fields.name: Veronica Falc├│n
fields.biography:
Ver├│nica Falc├│n┬á(born August 8, 1966) is a Mexican┬áactress┬áand┬áchoreographer. Regarding her English-speaking roles, she is best known for playing Camila Vargas in three seasons of┬áQueen of the South┬áand Lupe Gibbs in the 2020 HBO reboot of┬áPerry Mason. In 2022, Falc├│n played Camila Elizonndro (sister of cartel boss Omar Navarro) for Season 4 of┬áOzark.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Ver├│nica Falc├│n, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Bhasha Sumbli
fields.biography: Bhasha Sumbli is an Indian actress of Kashmiri Hindu (specifically Kashmiri Pandit) origin who is best known for her pivotal roles in the Hindi films The Kashmir Files and Baramulla.

fields.name: Gideon Emery
fields.biography:
ΓÇïFrom Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia. ┬á

Gideon Emery (born 12 September 1972) is an English actor and voice actor, known for his stage work in South Africa and for providing voices in video games. He lives in Los Angeles.

fields.name: Oh Se-yeong
fields.biography: Was a member of the Korean martial arts / stunt team Triple A.

fields.name: Lily Sullivan
fields.biography: Lily Sullivan is an Australian actress. She played Coral in the 2012 film Mental, and Miranda in the 2018 television series Picnic at Hanging Rock. She plays leading roles in two 2023 feature films, Australian sci-fi thriller Monolith, and American horror film Evil Dead Rise.

fields.name: James Wan
fields.biography:
James Wan (born 26 February 1977) is an Australian filmmaker. He has primarily worked in the horror genre as the co-creator of the Saw and Insidious franchises and the creator of The Conjuring Universe. The lattermost is the highest-grossing horror franchise at over $2 billion. Wan is also the founder of the film and television production company Atomic Monster.

Beginning his career with the Saw franchise, Wan made his feature directorial debut with his first film in 2004. The franchise became commercially successful and grossed more than $1 billion globally. Following a period of setbacks, Wan found new success with the Insidious series, in which he directed the first film in 2010 and its 2013 sequel. The same year as the second Insidious, Wan directed the first Conjuring film to critical and commercial success. He served as the director of the second installment in 2016 and produced subsequent films in the franchise.

Outside of horror, Wan directed Furious 7 (2015), the seventh installment of the Fast & Furious franchise, and the DC Extended Universe superhero films Aquaman (2018) and its sequel Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom (2023). Both Furious 7 and Aquaman grossed over $1 billion, making Wan the eighth director with two films to reach the milestone. He is the 16th highest-grossing director of all time as of 2021, with his films having grossed over $3.7 billion worldwide.

Description above from the Wikipedia article James Wan, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Lee Cronin
fields.biography: Lee Cronin (born 24 January 1982) is an Irish filmmaker. He is best known for directing horror films such as The Hole in the Ground (2019), Evil Dead Rise (2023), and Lee Cronin's The Mummy (2026).

fields.name: Jason Blum
fields.biography:
Jason Blum (born February 20, 1969) is an American film producer and the founder and CEO of Blumhouse Productions, the studio behind some of the most influential horror films of the 21st century. Under his leadership, Blumhouse produced the blockbuster franchises Paranormal Activity, Insidious, The Purge, and Halloween, helping redefine low-budget, high-impact genre filmmaking. BlumΓÇÖs producing credits also include Sinister, Oculus, Whiplash, The Gallows, The Gift, Hush, Split, Ouija: Origin of Evil, Get Out, Happy Death Day, Upgrade, Us, The Invisible Man, Freaky, The Black Phone, M3GAN, Five Nights at FreddyΓÇÖs, and Speak No Evil, spanning horror, thriller, and prestige drama.

He has received multiple Academy Awards Best Picture nominations for Whiplash, Get Out, and BlacKkKlansman. In television, Blum won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie for The Normal Heart and later earned an Emmy for Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Series for the acclaimed true-crime miniseries The Jinx.

fields.name: Emily Mitchell
fields.biography:
Emily Mitchell is a Canadian actress who has already made a name for herself working alongside some of the biggest names in Hollywood. Despite her young age, she has already appeared in several popular TV shows and movies, impressing audiences with her natural talent.

Emily is known for playing Miep Friesen in Sarah Polley's feature adaptation of Miriam Toews's best-selling novel Women Talking, Penny Brooks in Disney's Out of My Mind, Lisa Marie Presley in Sofia Coppola's biopic Priscilla and will star opposite Hilary Swank and Alan Ritchson in the Lionsgate drama Ordinary Angels, in theatres October 2023.

She also appears in CBS Ghosts, Disney FX What We Do in the Shadows, Apple TV+ Snoopy Presents: One-of-a-Kind Marcie and has several upcoming short films.

Emily has a number of exciting projects in the works.

fields.name: Macdara Kelleher
fields.biography: Macdara Kelleher is the CEO at Wild Atlantic Pictures.

fields.name: Judson Scott
fields.biography: Judson Scott is an American film producer and the Executive Vice President of Film at Atomic Monster.

fields.name: Michael Clear
fields.biography: Michael Clear is an American film producer and the Head of Film at Atomic Monster.

fields.name: Alayna Glasthal
fields.biography: Alayna Glasthal is the Creative Executive of Film at Atomic Monster.

fields.name: John Keville
fields.biography: John Keville is an Irish film producer. He is the co-founder of production companies Wild Atlantic Pictures and Doppelg├ñngers.

fields.name: Pete Chiappetta
fields.biography: Pete Chiappetta is a Managing Director and Portfolio Manager at Domain, where his primary role is managing the firmΓÇÖs Media, Entertainment, and Technology (MET) investment strategy.

fields.name: Andrew Lary
fields.biography:
Andrew Lary is a Partner and Executive Managing Director at Domain Capital, where he serves on the leadership team for the Media, Entertainment, and Technology (MET) business.

Since joining Domain in 2011, Andrew has been a key force in the firmΓÇÖs exponential growth, with assets under management rising from $1.2 billion to nearly $8 billion. He spearheaded the expansion of the business beyond its real estate roots into the MET sector, co-leading the origination of $1.5 billion in investments, including $800 million in entertainment assets. In 2020, he was instrumental in launching the firmΓÇÖs Entertainment fund, which successfully secured over $700 million in investor commitments.

Andrew began his career in 1995 with PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), where he advanced to Senior Manager in the Real Estate Business Advisory Services division over the course of eight years. There, he provided strategic management and consultative services to major financial institutions. In 2003, he continued this work through Sandusky Capital, a firm he cofounded.

He holds a B.S.M. in Accounting from Tulane University and is a Certified Public Accountant licensed in New York (inactive). In addition to his professional responsibilities, Andrew serves on numerous advisory boards on behalf of DomainΓÇÖs clients.

fields.name: Anthony Tittanegro
fields.biography:
Anthony Tittanegro is a Partner and Executive Managing Director at Domain Capital.

He joined Domain in 2010. Before his tenure at Domain, Anthony founded and operated Titan Property Group, a boutique real estate investment and development firm. He also spent 11 years with PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) in their Real Estate Advisory practice, and six years in service with Prudential.

In addition to his professional pursuits, Anthony is a member of the Counsellors of Real Estate Organisation and serves on the Board of Directors of Midcap Financial, a speciality finance company with approximately $40 billion in assets under management. He completed his B.S. in Business Finance at the Florida Institute of Technology. He earned his masterΓÇÖs degree from New York University.

fields.name: Jennifer Scudder Trent
fields.biography: Jennifer Scudder Trent is an American film producer at Blumhouse Productions. She is best known for producing the films The Invisible Man (2020), Freaky (2020), The Black Phone (2021), M3GAN (2022), The Exorcist: Believer (2023), Five Nights at Freddy's (2023), Speak No Evil (2024) and Wolf Man (2025).

fields.name: Terri Taylor
fields.biography: Over the course of her extensive career in casting, Terri Taylor has worked on over 50 feature films. TheyΓÇÖve ranged from big studio releases to surprise gems from the independent film world. She has worked with acclaimed directors, such as Steven Spielberg, Jordan Peele, Damien Chazelle, and Jon M. Chu, among several others.

fields.name: Nick Bassett
fields.biography: Nick Bassett (born 9 November 1970) is a New Zealand production designer and art director.

fields.name: Peter Albrechtsen
fields.biography: Peter Albrechtsen is an award-winning Danish sound designer and re-recording mixer working on both Scandinavian and international movies.

fields.name: Jack Black
fields.biography:
Thomas Jacob Black┬á(born August 28, 1969) is an American actor, comedian, and musician. He is known for his roles in family and comedy films and his voice work in animated films. His awards include a┬áChildren's and Family Emmy Award, a┬áGrammy Award, and three┬áGolden Globe Award nominations.

After portraying supporting roles in films including┬áDead Man Walking┬á(1995),┬áThe Cable Guy (1996),┬áMars Attacks!┬á(1996), and┬áEnemy of the State┬á(1998), Black had his breakout role in the musical film┬áHigh Fidelity┬á(2000). This led to larger roles in films like┬áShallow Hal┬á(2001) and┬áOrange County┬á(2002) before he solidified his leading-man status with his starring role in┬áSchool of Rock┬á(2003). Black has since starred in┬áKing Kong┬á(2005),┬áThe Holiday┬á(2006),┬áNacho Libre (2006),┬áTropic Thunder┬á(2008),┬áBernie┬á(2011),┬áGoosebumps┬á(2016),┬áand Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle┬á(2017), its sequel┬áJumanji: The Next Level (2019), The House with a Clock in Its Walls (2018) and┬áA Minecraft Movie┬á(2025). He has also voiced┬áPo┬áin the┬áKung Fu Panda┬áfranchise (2008ΓÇôpresent) and┬áBowser┬áin┬áThe Super Mario Bros. Movie franchise┬á(2023ΓÇôpresent).┬á

Black is the lead vocalist of the duo┬áTenacious D, which he formed in 1994 with long-time friend┬áKyle Gass. In 2015, they won the Grammy Award for best metal performance for "The Last in Line." Since 2018, Black has run a YouTube channel called Jablinski Games.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Jack Black, licensed under CC-BY-SA; full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Brie Larson
fields.biography:
Brianne Sidonie Desaulniers┬á(born October 1, 1989), known professionally as┬áBrie Larson, is an American actress. She played supporting roles in comedies as a teenager and has since expanded to leading roles in┬áindependent films┬áand┬áblockbusters.┬áHer accolades┬áinclude an┬áAcademy Award, a┬áGolden Globe Award, and a┬áPrimetime Emmy Award.┬áTime┬ámagazine named her one of the┬á100 most influential people in the world┬áin 2019.

At age six, Larson was the youngest student admitted to a training program at the┬áAmerican Conservatory Theater, and she began her acting career in 1998 with a┬ácomedy sketch┬áon┬áThe Tonight Show with Jay Leno. She appeared as a regular on the sitcom┬áRaising Dad┬á(2001ΓÇô2002). She pursued a music career, releasing the album┬áFinally Out of P.E.┬á(2005). She subsequently had supporting roles in the comedy films┬áHoot (2006),┬áScott Pilgrim vs. the World┬á(2010), and┬á21 Jump Street┬á(2012), and appeared as a sardonic teenager in the television series┬áUnited States of Tara┬á(2009ΓÇô2011).

Larson's breakthrough came as a social worker in the independent drama┬áShort Term 12┬á(2013), along with supporting roles in the coming-of-age romance┬áThe Spectacular Now┬á(2013) and the comedy┬áTrainwreck┬á(2015). She gained wider recognition for her performance as a kidnapping victim in the drama┬áRoom┬á(2015), for which she received the┬áAcademy Award for Best Actress. She ventured into┬áblockbusters┬áwith the monster film┬áKong: Skull Island┬á(2017) and by starring as┬áCarol Danvers / Captain Marvel┬áin the┬áMarvel Cinematic Universe, beginning with┬áCaptain Marvel (2019). Larson returned to television to star in the miniseries┬áLessons in Chemistry┬á(2023), for which she earned a nomination for the┬áPrimetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress.

Larson has co-written and co-directed two short films and made her feature film directorial debut with the independent comedy-drama┬áUnicorn Store┬á(2017). For producing the┬ávirtual reality┬áseries┬áThe Messy Truth VR Experience┬á(2020), she won a┬áPrimetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Interactive Program. A┬ágender equality┬áactivist and an advocate for┬ásexual assault┬ásurvivors, Larson is vocal about social and political issues.

fields.name: Keegan-Michael Key
fields.biography:
Keegan-Michael Key (born March 22, 1971) is an American actor and comedian, best known for starring in the Comedy Central sketch series Key & Peele and for his six seasons as a cast member on MADtv. He has also appeared in the films Wonka, Toy Story 4, and Pitch Perfect 2.

Key was born in Southfield, Michigan and raised in Detroit. His father is African-American and his mother is European-American. He was adopted as a child. In 1989 he graduated from Shrine Catholic High School in Royal Oak, Michigan. Key attended the University of Detroit as an undergraduate and earned his Master of Fine Arts at the Pennsylvania State University School of Theatre. While at The University of Detroit Mercy, he was a brother of Phi Kappa Theta.

fields.name: Glen Powell
fields.biography:
Glen Thomas Powell Jr.┬á(born October 21, 1988) is an American actor. He began his career with minor roles on television and in films such as┬áSpy Kids 3-D: Game Over┬á(2003) and┬áFast Food Nation┬á(2006). Powell acted in the action film┬áThe Expendables 3┬á(2014), the comedy-horror anthology series┬áScream Queens┬á(2015ΓÇô2016), the teen comedy┬áEverybody Wants Some!!┬á(2016), the historical romance┬áThe Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society (2018), and the romantic comedy┬áSet It Up (2018). He also portrayed astronaut┬áJohn Glenn in┬áHidden Figures┬á(2016) and aviator┬áTom Hudner in┬áDevotion┬á(2022).

Powell's roles in the action film┬áTop Gun: Maverick (2022) and the romantic comedy┬áAnyone but You┬á(2023) catapulted him to blockbuster stardom. He has since starred in the dark comedy┬áHit Man (2023), which he also co-wrote and produced, and in the disaster film┬áTwisters┬á(2024). His performance in the former earned him a Golden Globe Award nomination.

Further, Powell starred in Edgar Wright's The Running Man (2025), based on the 1987 Stephen King novella of the same name; How to Make a Killing (2026), a remake of the 1949 film Kind Hearts and Coronets; and had his first major voice performance in a feature film as Fox McCloud (aka Star Fox) in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (2026), a role he personally sought Nintendo for.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Glen Powell, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Luis Guzm├ín
fields.biography: Luis Guzm├ín (born August 28, 1956) is a Puerto Rico-American actor. He is known for his character work. For much of his career, his squat build, wolfish features, and brooding countenance have garnered him roles largely as sidekicks, thugs, or policemen, but his later career has seen him move into more mainstream roles. He is a favorite of director Steven Soderbergh, who cast him in Out of Sight, The Limey, and Traffic, and Paul Thomas Anderson, who cast him in Boogie Nights, Magnolia and Punch-Drunk Love. He also voiced Ricardo Diaz in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories.

fields.name: Issa Rae
fields.biography:
JoIssa Rae Diop (born January 12, 1985), known professionally as┬áIssa Rae, is an American actress, writer, and producer. She achieved recognition as the co-creator, co-writer, and star of the┬áHBO┬ácomedy series┬áInsecure (2016ΓÇô2021), for which she was nominated for multiple┬áGolden Globes Awards┬áand┬áPrimetime Emmy Awards.

Rae first garnered attention for her work on the┬áYouTube┬áweb series┬áAwkward Black Girl┬á(2011ΓÇô2013).┬áHer 2015 memoir, ┬áThe Misadventures of Awkward Black Girl, became a┬áNew York Times┬ábestseller. In 2020, Rae formed the production company┬áHoorae Media.

Rae has also appeared in films, with roles in the drama┬áThe Hate U Give┬á(2018), the fantasy comedy┬áLittle┬á(2019), the romance┬áThe Photograph┬á(2020), the romantic comedy┬áThe Lovebirds┬á(2020), the comedy thriller┬áVengeance(2022), and the comedies┬áBarbie┬áand┬áAmerican Fiction┬á(both 2023). She also had a voice role in the short film┬áHair Love┬á(2019) and voiced┬áJess Drew / Spider-Woman┬áin┬áSpider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse┬á(2023).

In 2018 and 2022, Rae was included in the annual┬áTime┬á100 list of the most influential people in the world┬áand in 2014 in the┬áForbes '30 Under 30'┬álist in the entertainment section. She was recognized with the┬áPeabody Trailblazer Award┬áand the┬áProducers Guild of America Visionary Award.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Issa Rae, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Kevin Michael Richardson
fields.biography: Kevin Michael Richardson (born October 25, 1964) is an American actor and voice artist who currently stars in The Cleveland Show. He is also well known for being the voice of Enclave communications officer and Tartarus in the video games Fallout 2 and Halo  2.
fields.place_of_birth: The Bronx, New York City, New York, USA

fields.name: Chris Pratt
fields.biography:
Christopher Michael Pratt (born 21 June 1979) is an American actor, known for starring in both television and action films. He rose to prominence for his television roles, particularly in the NBC sitcom Parks and Recreation (2009ΓÇô2015), for which he received critical acclaim and was nominated for the Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series in 2013. He also starred earlier in his career as Bright Abbott in The WB drama series Everwood (2002ΓÇô2006) and had roles in Wanted (2008), Jennifer's Body (2009), Moneyball (2011), The Five-Year Engagement (2012), Zero Dark Thirty (2013), Delivery Man (2013), and Her (2013).

Pratt achieved leading man status in 2014, starring in two critically and commercially successful films: The Lego Movie as Emmet Brickowski, and Marvel Studios' Guardians of the Galaxy as Star-Lord. He starred in Jurassic World (2015) and Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom (2018), and he reprised his Marvel role in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017), Avengers: Infinity War (2018), Avengers: Endgame (2019), and the planned Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3. Meanwhile, in 2016 he was part of an ensemble cast in The Magnificent Seven and the male lead in Passengers.

Description above is from the Wikipedia article Chris Pratt, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

fields.name: Juliet Jelenic
fields.biography: Juliet Jelenic is the daughter of animator Michael Jelenic. She voiced Lumalee in The Super Mario Bros. Movie and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, both of which her father directed.

fields.name: Carlos Alazraqui
fields.biography: Carlos Jaime Alazraqui (born July 20, 1962) is an American actor, stand-up comedian, impressionist and voice actor. He is best known for his role as Deputy James Garcia on the Comedy Central series Reno 911!. His voice-over work includes the role of Bobbi Fabulous on Phineas and Ferb, the Taco Bell chihuahua, Denzel Q. Crocker and Juandissimo Magnifico on The Fairly OddParents!, Rocko on Rocko's Modern Life, Lazlo in Camp Lazlo, and as Jonathan Weed on Family Guy.

fields.name: Eric Bauza
fields.biography: Eric Bauza is a Canadian-American voice actor and comedian. His roles include Stimpy on Ren and Stimpy "Adult Party Cartoon", Rodolfo Rivera/White Pantera on El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera, Foop on The Fairly OddParents, Lord Stingray on Superjail!, Chairman Drek from the 2016 Ratchet & Clank game, the Beagle Boys on DuckTales, Master Frown on Unikitty!, Flip Champion on Ballmastrz: 9009 and Leonardo in Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. He is one of the current voices of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian, Pep├⌐ Le Pew, Tweety, Speedy Gonzales, Henery Hawk, Barnyard Dawg, Sylvester Jr., Woody Woodpecker, Boo-Boo Bear, Atom Ant, Luke Skywalker, and Dino.

fields.name: Charlie Endean
fields.biography:
Charlie Endean is a British film and television first assistant director. He earned a First-Class Bachelor of Arts degree in Film, Cinema, and Video Studies from the University of the Arts London in 2005.

Early in his career, Endean built a strong foundation in television, contributing as first assistant director to series like The Midnight Beast (2012),┬áTatau (2015),┬áHumans (2015),┬áThe Last Kingdom (2015), and┬áVikings (2017-2019). His work on┬áGame of Thrones┬áduring seasons 6 and 7, particularly on the pivotal episodes "Battle of the Bastards," "The Winds of Winter," "Spoils of War," and "Eastwatch," earned praise for his ability to coordinate large-scale action, intricate set pieces, and complex logistics. In interviews, he described his role as the nexus between a director's vision and production constraints, responsible for script breakdowns, scheduling, and aligning departments such as set design, stunts, digital effects, and extrasΓÇöa role he likened to keeping "the machine moving fast" while preserving creative integrity.

In film, Endean has worked as first assistant director on major theatrical features including┬áSergio┬á(2020),┬áThe Lost City (2022), and┬áJurassic World: Dominion┬á(2022), where he also served in an associate producer capacity on the latter two.

fields.name: Charlie Day
fields.biography:
Charles Peckham Day (born February 9, 1976) is an American actor, writer, and producer. He is best known for playing Charlie Kelly on the FX/FXX dark comedy It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (2005ΓÇôpresent), of which he is also a writer and an executive producer. In 2011, he was nominated for a Critics' Choice Television Award and a Satellite Award for the role. Subsequently, he co-created the Apple TV+ comedy Mythic Quest (2020ΓÇô2025) with Rob Mac and Megan Ganz.

In film, Day is best known for his performances as Dr. Newton Geiszler in Guillermo del Toro's Pacific Rim (2013), Dale Arbus in the comedy Horrible Bosses (2011) and its sequel Horrible Bosses 2 (2014), and Andy Campbell in the comedy Fist Fight (2017). He is also known for his voice roles in Monsters University (2013), The Lego Movie film franchise (2014ΓÇô2019) and Nintendo franchise character Luigi in The Super Mario Bros. Movie (2023) and its sequel, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (2026). He made his directorial debut with Fool's Paradise (2023).

Description above from the Wikipedia article Charlie Day, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
fields.place_of_birth: New York City, New York, USA

fields.name: Scott Menville
fields.biography: Scott David Menville (born February 12, 1971) is an American actor, voice actor and musician. He is best known for his voice work in animated films and television series.

fields.name: Anya Taylor-Joy
fields.biography:
Anya-Josephine Marie Taylor-Joy┬á(/╦ê├ªnj╔Ö/; born 16 April 1996) is an actress. Born in Miami and raised in Buenos Aires and London, she left school at 16 to pursue an acting career. After several minor television roles, her┬ábreakthrough came with a leading role in the horror film┬áThe Witch┬á(2015). Her career progressed with roles in the horror film┬áSplit┬á(2016) and its sequel┬áGlass┬á(2019), the black comedy film┬áThoroughbreds┬á(2017), and playing┬áEmma Woodhouse┬áin the period drama┬áEmma┬á(2020).┬á

Taylor-Joy featured in the television crime drama series┬áPeaky Blinders┬á(2019ΓÇô2022) and earned international recognition for playing┬áBeth Harmon┬áin the period drama miniseries┬áThe Queen's Gambit┬á(2020), winning a┬áGolden Globe Award┬áand a┬áSAG Award, in addition to a nomination for a┬áPrimetime Emmy Award. She then starred in the horror film┬áLast Night in Soho┬á(2021), the action films┬áThe Northman┬á(2022) and┬áThe Gorge┬á(2025), and the black comedy┬áThe Menu┬á(2022). She also voiced┬áPrincess Peach┬áin the animated film┬áThe Super Mario Bros. Movie┬á(2023). She starred as┬áImperator Furiosa┬áin the apocalyptic film┬áFuriosa: A Mad Max Saga┬á(2024).
